extracted.intended_audience: Mathematics Stack Exchange users writing questions, answers, and comments
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing and formatting posts on Mathematics Stack Exchange using the visual editor, Markdown, and a subset of HTML; includes rules for comments and images. Targeted at users creating questions and answers (not comments which have restricted formatting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed editors and formats
rubrics_metrics.description: When posting on Mathematics Stack Exchange, you can use the visual editor (for questions and answers, but not comments), Markdown, and some HTML.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you're new to Markdown, you may want to visit the official Markdown syntax reference page. More details are available on the advanced editing help page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linebreaks and paragraphs
rubrics_metrics.description:
End a line with two spaces to add a
linebreak. New paragraphs only occur when there is a blank line. A single carriage does not create a new paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'How do I love thee?  (two spaces)\nLet me count the ways' produces a line break. Use a blank line between paragraphs to start a new paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Italics and bold
rubrics_metrics.description: Use *this* or _this_ for italics; use **this** or __this__ for bold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can combine them: use ***italics and bold together*** if you ___have to___.

rubrics_metrics.name: Links — inline, reference-style, and readable links
rubrics_metrics.description: There are three ways to write links: inline ([text](url)), reference-style ([text][id]) with a separate definition, and readable links using a reference name ([text][name]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Here's an inline link to [Google](https://www.google.com/). Here's a reference-style link to [Google][1]. Here's a very readable link to [Yahoo!][yahoo]. Link definitions can appear anywhere in the document — before or after the place where you use them. The link definition names can be any unique string and are case-insensitive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Link definitions and naming
rubrics_metrics.description: Link definition names (the reference labels) can be any unique string and are case-insensitive; definitions may appear before or after usage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example definitions: [1]: https://www.google.com/  [yahoo]: https://www.yahoo.com/ . [yahoo] is the same as [YAHOO].

rubrics_metrics.name: Advanced link attributes and best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Links can have a title attribute which shows on hover, and standard HTML hyperlink syntax is also allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Here's a [poorly-named link](https://www.google.com/ "Google"). Never write 'click here' — use descriptive link text instead (see linked W3C advice). You can also write links using HTML: example.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bulleted lists syntax
rubrics_metrics.description: Create bulleted lists using -, +, or * at the start of the line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: '- Use a minus sign for a bullet', '+ Or plus sign', '* Or an asterisk'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbered lists and automatic numbering
rubrics_metrics.description: Numbered lists use numeric markers and Markdown keeps track of the numbers for you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: you can write '1.' and '2.' and then '7.' and Markdown will render them as items 1, 2, 3 respectively (7 will become item 3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph-wrapped (double-spaced) list items
rubrics_metrics.description:
If you leave a blank line between list items, the items will be wrapped in

tags, causing extra space between items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows a double-spaced list where an empty line between items produces extra space in rendered output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blockquotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Create blockquotes by adding a '>' at the beginning of a line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The syntax is based on email quoting; you don't need to hard-wrap paragraphs in blockquotes, but it looks nicer if you do. (The page notes: 'Depends how lazy you feel.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Tag mention formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: To refer to a tag on the site, use [tag:tagname], which will automatically link to the tag info page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'See the many questions tagged [tag:elephants] to learn more.' The tag will automatically be linked to the corresponding tag info page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment formatting limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments support only bold, italic, inline code (backticks), and links; in addition, a few shorthand links are available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supported inline formatting: _italic_ and **bold**, inline `code in backticks`, and basic links. Comments do not support full Markdown/HTML features like images or blockquotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supported comment shorthand links and their behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments accept several shorthand link tokens that expand to particular destinations: [meta], [edit], [tag:tagname], [meta-tag:tagname], [about], [help], [chat].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Behavior details: [meta] links to the current site's Meta (no-op if none); [edit] links to the edit page for the post (link text 'edit'); [tag:tagname] and [meta-tag:tagname] link to the tag page (meta-tag only works on meta sites); [about] links to the About page; [help] links to the Help Center; [chat] links to the current site's chat site (link text '{site name} Chat'). For more shorthand links see the expanded formatting guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Images — insertion methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Images can be added primarily via the editor toolbar button which uploads images through the imgur hosting service (including from the clipboard); alternatively use HTML or Markdown image syntax.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HTML example: . Markdown example: ![sample image](https://example.com/img.jpg). The toolbar provides a special interface to upload images.
